items.mainDefect: The jsforce Connection is still built with the old access_token and instance_url, even after a new token has been fetched and saved.

secondary.defect: The old refresh_token is saved again and passed to jsforce, even though the manual refresh may have rotated it, which breaks jsforce's own fallback refresh.

items.mainDefect: The computed-key 'index signature' in minimumTokenResponseSchema becomes the literal key "[object Object]", so zod removes the expiry field and keeps only access_token.

secondary.defect: When a response has no refresh_token, the placeholder string "refresh_token" is saved into the credential.

items.mainDefect: The comments on minimumTokenResponseSchema describe catch-all and expiry behaviour that the code does not actually have.

secondary.defect: The computed keys collapse to "[object Object]" and z.object removes unknown keys, so the expiry in the sync response is silently dropped.

items.mainDefect: The computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema do not create an index signature, so zod removes every field except access_token and the expiry is lost.

secondary.defect: The literal string "refresh_token" is put into the parsed data when the response has none, and office365calendar then saves it over the real refresh token.

items.mainDefect: An invalid webhook body makes appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throw a ZodError that is never caught, so the caller gets a 500 instead of a 400.

secondary.defect: symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse throw on keys that are not valid encrypted JSON, and the error is never caught, so the caller gets a 500 instead of a 400.
